---
title: "R13. Putting figures into the public domain"
description: "Intelligent transparency, being open about how a result was reached, and where NHSBSA publishes analysis."
---

Publishing a figure puts it beyond your control. This page carries what that asks of you, and
where NHSBSA analysis is published.

## Intelligent transparency

The Code of Practice for Statistics sets out **intelligent transparency**: taking an open, clear and accessible approach to the use of data, statistics and wider analysis in
the public domain. It is the default, not a decision to be made each time.


**It binds more than official statistics.** The Code's Standards for the Public Use of Statistics, Data and Wider Analysis apply to public
bodies using statistics, data and wider analysis in the public domain. They apply to everyone
involved in that use, not to analysts alone. A figure quoted
in a press release, a board paper made public, or a number given to a journalist is in scope. There
are three standards.[^src-code-of-practice-for-statistics-edition-3-0-standards-for-the-public-use-of-statistics-data-and-wider-analysis]

**1. Equality of access.** Make what is used in the public domain available to everyone in a timely
way, so the public can access, scrutinise and verify the claims made from it.

- draw on the latest and most reliable published official statistics where possible
- publish the figures **in advance of, or at the same time as**, their use in public communications
- publish them **separately from** any related policy or ministerial statement
- if unpublished figures are referred to publicly, publish them as soon as possible, ideally the
  same day

**2. Supporting understanding.** Use figures with integrity and communicate them with clarity and
accuracy, so the public can understand the basis for the claims made.

- do not cherry-pick figures, take them out of context, or place undue certainty on them
- communicate the key context and limitations alongside them
- be clear where the figures came from, citing sources in publications and on social media
- take proactive steps to prevent or minimise misinterpretation and misuse

**3. Decision making and leadership.** Seek and use impartial, expert advice when using figures in
the public domain.

::: {.callout-important title="The one that catches people out" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
Quoting an unpublished number in public starts a clock. Under equality of access it should be
published as soon as possible, ideally the same day, because until it is published nobody can check
the claim made from it.

If an analysis is going to be quoted before it is published, that is a conversation to have while
the analysis is being scoped, not after the quotation appears.
:::

## Transparency of the analysis itself

Beyond algorithmic tools, transparency means the ordinary discipline of being open about how a
result was reached:

- the assurance level applied, and why. See
  [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd)
- the quality assurance statement. See
  [Phase 4, delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd)
- the data sources, extract dates and known quality issues
- the code, published where it can be

For official statistics, the Code's ten standards apply as well as the three standards above.
Standard 4 requires producers to manage data safely and securely, and to be open about how it will
be used and protected. Standard 1 requires them to challenge misuse. See
[the standards landscape](r8-the-standards-landscape.qmd).

## Where NHSBSA analysis is published

| Output | Published at |
|---|---|
| Official statistics | [NHSBSA statistical collections](https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/statistical-collections) |
| Research and insight articles | [NHSBSA data science projects](https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/data-science-projects) |
| Open datasets | [NHSBSA Open Data Portal](https://opendata.nhsbsa.net/) |
| Analytical code | [NHSBSA data and analytics code repositories](https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/data-and-analytics-code-repositories) |
